definition: Automatically generating programs that satisfy a specification — examples, types, or natural language — from inductive programming to LLM code generation.
details: Automatically generating programs that satisfy a specification — examples, types, or natural language — from inductive programming to LLM code generation.

explainer.lead: Program synthesis automatically generates programs that satisfy a given specification, whether that is examples, types, or natural language. It matters because it shifts program creation from hand-writing code to specifying intent.

tiers.eli5: Instead of writing every line of code yourself, you show the computer what you want the program to do, and it writes the program for you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use program synthesis with specifications ranging from input-output examples and type constraints to natural-language descriptions. A pitfall is that the specification must be precise enough to pin down the intended behavior.
tiers.paperLevel: Program synthesis is the automatic generation of programs satisfying a specification, spanning inductive programming (from examples) to LLM-based code generation from natural language. Its limit is that correctness is bounded by how well the specification captures intent.

explainer.example: A user provides a handful of input-output examples, and a synthesis system generates a program that reproduces those outputs and generalizes to new inputs.
